perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- Keith and Elizabeth are colleagues at the construction company; he is a construction worker and she is the receptionist. They interact for paperwork/project updates and have a friendly but professional relationship.
- Recently, Keith noticed Elizabeth being unusually curt with him over several days.
- Keith suspected he might have upset her through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake, so he asked her directly.
- Elizabeth told him she was not upset with him; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and told her he understood she was going through a tough time. He offered to listen and suggested a coffee break.
- Elizabeth accepted, said that was kind, and thanked him.
- Over coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as severe.
- Keith thanked her for sharing and asked whether she had considered talking to a professional, saying an outside perspective can help.
- Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He worried he might have overstepped or embarrassed her, and he told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what.
- Elizabeth told him he hadn’t overstepped, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed that Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative.
- Keith told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available if she needed to chat or take a break together.
- Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot to her, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith believes Elizabeth values his support and feels more comfortable around him, and he intends to maintain a supportive relationship with her.
